definitions.explanation: A one-sided tendency or prejudice in thinking, reporting, or attitudes. Often used critically to point out unfairness or lack of objectivity.

examples.japanese: {偏向|へんこう}{報道|ほうどう}だと{批判|ひはん}された。
examples.english: It was criticized as biased reporting.

examples.japanese: あのメディアは{政治的|せいじてき}に{偏向|へんこう}している。
examples.english: That media outlet is politically biased.

examples.japanese: {偏向|へんこう}した{見方|みかた}ではなく、{多角的|たかくてき}な{視点|してん}で{物事|ものごと}を{判断|はんだん}すべきだ。
examples.english: One should judge matters from multiple perspectives, not from a biased viewpoint.

notes:
Composed of {偏|へん} (one-sided, biased) + {向|こう} (direction, inclination). Carries a negative connotation — it implies that something is unfairly tilted in one direction. Most commonly encountered in media criticism.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {偏向|へんこう}{報道|ほうどう}: biased reporting
- {偏向|へんこう}{教育|きょういく}: biased education; ideological indoctrination
- {偏向|へんこう}した{意見|いけん}: a biased opinion
- {偏向|へんこう}する: to be biased; to lean

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {偏見|へんけん}: prejudice (about personal beliefs and attitudes toward people)
- バイアス: bias (loanword; common in academic/technical contexts)
- {先入観|せんにゅうかん}: preconceived notion (emphasis on pre-existing assumptions)
